name: Telehouse

profile.address: 7, Teleport Drive, Staten Island, Richmond County, New York, 10314
profile.reading:
Telehouse's New York Teleport facility occupies a 162,000 square foot building at 7 Teleport Drive on the West Shore of Staten Island, inside an office and telecommunications park that took its name from its original purpose as a satellite teleport serving the New York region. The Teleport park was developed in the 1980s around satellite earth station infrastructure meant to give New York area broadcasters and carriers direct access to satellite uplinks, and the Telehouse building was one of the first facilities there to anchor that development with a fiber and colocation offering rather than a purely satellite based one. The building opened in 1989, making it one of the longest continuously operating carrier and colocation facilities in the New York metropolitan market, predating most of the purpose built data centers that now cluster in New Jersey and around Manhattan's core network meet me points. It has operated throughout under the Telehouse brand, a data center and network services company that is a subsidiary of Japan's KDDI Corporation and runs a global chain of facilities built around telecommunications carrier neutrality.

Telehouse's own materials for the site describe standby power as six diesel generators totaling 5,625 kVA, configured N plus 1, a sizable backup generation base for a building of this footprint. The same materials separately state that 10 megawatts of total power is available at the facility and that individual cabinets can be provisioned up to a maximum of 20 kilowatts, though the published materials do not make clear whether either figure represents power currently drawn by tenants, capacity reserved for future growth, or simply a ceiling on what a single cabinet could be provisioned to rather than a typical operating density. This profile reports them as published figures rather than confirmed operating loads. Telehouse does not publish current occupancy, a named tenant list, or any third party facility certification, such as an Uptime Institute tier rating, for the New York Teleport building.

Staten Island's relative distance from Manhattan's densest carrier hotels has historically made this facility more of a secondary interconnection point for the region than buildings located directly in lower Manhattan or across the river in New Jersey, but its age, its diesel generation capacity, and its continuous operation under one well known international operator for more than three decades make it a stable and long standing part of the New York area's telecommunications and data center landscape.

profile.corporate_note: Subsidiary of KDDI Corporation (Japan). Recent M&A: KDDI/Telehouse acquired Allied Properties' data center portfolio (~$1B, per DataCenterDynamics trade press).

reading:
Telehouse is a carrier neutral colocation operator and part of the KDDI group of Japan. Telehouse America was established in 1987 under its first president, Dr. Yasuo Fukata, and the facility this registry holds, the New York Teleport data centre at 7 Teleport Drive on Staten Island, became operational in 1989. Telehouse is in a data centre registry for the ordinary reason that it sells space and power to other companies, but its commercial argument has always been interconnection rather than scale. It launched the New York International Internet Exchange in 1996 at its Manhattan Center, added exchange points at 60 Hudson Street in 2003 and 111 Eighth Avenue in 2005, and in 2007 added further NYIIX connection points in Staten Island, Manhattan and Newark.

Telehouse publishes an unusually complete specification for the Teleport building, which makes it a good illustration of why power figures have to be labelled. The site is 162,000 square feet. It has redundant commercial power feeds with 10 MW total available, which is utility service the building can draw. It has static A and B uninterruptible power supply systems rated up to 4,700 kVA in N+1 configuration, which is a UPS rating. It has six diesel generators totalling 5,625 kVA in N+1 with a 48 hour on site fuel supply, which is standby generation. It has eight battery strings able to carry full load for up to 15 minutes. None of those is a critical IT load, and Telehouse does not publish one. The company markets up to 20 kW per cabinet, two diverse fibre routes into the site and peering up to 100 Gigabit Ethernet, and states that the building has never lost critical power since it opened.

The land under it has a public record of its own. The Teleport sits inside the Staten Island Industrial Park, a roughly 415 acre city owned property managed by the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey under lease, as documented in New York City Planning Commission material. The Port Authority selected the site in 1981 for what was promoted as the country's first worldwide satellite communications centre. Contemporary reporting in 1983 put the project at $300 million across two five year phases, with 17 aluminium dishes about 25 feet across reaching 24 domestic and international satellites and more than a million square feet of office space in the first phase. AT&T became the largest tenant and left in 2001, the satellite antennas have since been removed, and the campus now reads as an office and data processing park. Telehouse's building is the part of it that stayed in the business the site was originally built for.
